Paper Title: Early Detection of Diabetes Mellitus Using Machine Learning Techniques
Strengths: Comparative evaluation of traditional classifiers with CV and sensible baselines.
Limitations: Limited features (Pima-only); no deep learning or XAI considered.

Paper Title: Diabetes Prediction Using Logistic Regression and Machine Learning Techniques
Dataset Used: Pima Indian Diabetes Dataset / Clinical registry
Algorithms / Models Used: Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest
Strengths: Clear presentation of LR as interpretable baseline; robust cross-validation.
Limitations: Limited external validation; does not explore DL or formal XAI methods.

Paper Title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Diabetes Risk Using Clinical Data
Algorithms / Models Used: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression
Strengths: Large-scale clinical validation; attention to feature engineering and calibration.
Limitations: Limited exploration of deep learning architectures and XAI for individual-level explanations.

Paper Title: Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Diabetes Prediction
Dataset Used: Pima Indian Diabetes Dataset / Combined clinical datasets
Algorithms / Models Used: SVM, Random Forest, KNN, Logistic Regression
Accuracy / Performance: ~0.79-0.85 depending on method; SVM/RF top performers
Strengths: Broad algorithm comparison and sensitivity analysis.
Limitations: Often limited to small datasets; no model interpretability module.

Paper Title: Random Forest-Based Predictive Model for Type 2 Diabetes
Strengths: Interpretable variable importance; robust handling of tabular data.
Limitations: Feature importance is global; lacks per-instance explanations and DL exploration.

Paper Title: Diabetes Prediction Using Support Vector Machines
Strengths: Thorough treatment of kernel methods and regularization.
Limitations: Scalability and interpretability are limited for clinicians.

Paper Title: Deep Learning Approaches for Diabetes Prediction Using Electronic Health Records
Accuracy / Performance: ~0.86 accuracy; AUC ~0.90 for well-tuned DL models
Strengths: Captures temporal patterns in EHR; improved performance on large data.
Limitations: Challenge in interpretability; requires substantial data and compute.

Paper Title: IoT and Machine Learning-Based System for Monitoring Diabetes
Dataset Used: Sensor streams + clinical records; research demo datasets
Algorithms / Models Used: Random Forest, SVM, lightweight Neural Nets
Strengths: Real-time monitoring pipeline; emphasis on reliability and edge inferencing.
Limitations: Data heterogeneity and privacy concerns; limited interpretability.

Paper Title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Diabetes Risk Prediction Using SHAP
Algorithms / Models Used: XGBoost/Gradient Boosting, Random Forest; SHAP for explanation
Accuracy / Performance: ~0.85-0.89 AUC with SHAP explanations for model trust
Strengths: Per-instance SHAP explanations allow clinical plausibility checks and feature-level transparency.
Limitations: SHAP computation can be costly; explains post-hoc, not inherently interpretable models.

Paper Title: Interpretable Machine Learning Models in Healthcare Diagnostics
Dataset Used: Survey across multiple clinical datasets (N/A specific)
Algorithms / Models Used: Survey: LR, SVM, RF, DL, XAI methods (LIME/SHAP)
Strengths: Comprehensive literature synthesis and taxonomy of interpretability methods.
Limitations: Survey-level conclusions; does not present new empirical results.

Dataset Used: PIMA Indian Diabetes Dataset + additional clinical features (local clinical registry)
Algorithms / Models Used: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, LSTM, GRU, CNN
Accuracy / Performance: Best models: RF ~0.87; CNN/LSTM ~0.89; AUC up to 0.92 in cross-validation
Strengths: Multi-model pipeline including classical ML and deep learning; integrated per-instance XAI (SHAP/LIME); deployment as Streamlit web app for clinical accessibility.
Limitations: PIMA dataset <--> real-world heterogeneity; needs external multi-center validation; deployment privacy/hardening tasks remain.
